name: The sentence that carries it
inputs: one row with a verified anchor the memo leans on (anchor, doc, locus)
shape: The anchor sentence set large in the margin beside the paragraph that leans on it, with the text and page it comes from; only verified anchors qualify.
didactic: The author's own words at the point where the memo makes its claim.
example: 'There are two Marxian models of the transition from feudalism to capitalism … they are entirely incompatible' beside the joined verdict.

evidence.note: the quoted sentence stops before stating anything about the second model or the culmination claim it is meant to anchor
the quoted fragment states no complete claim, defeating the exhibit's aim of showing the conclusion in the author's words
the exhibit has no content and the prose itself flags it as unfulfilled
